mbm-0443.clue: I can tell a kite from a kettle.
mbm-0443.quote: At our favorite lookout my friend mistook a distant bird of prey for a puff of steam from his cup. I handed him the binoculars. The kite wheeled in a perfect circle and the tea went quite cold.

mbm-0444.clue: My first bowling trophy plugs into the wall.
mbm-0444.quote: I bought a worn bowling pin at an alley auction and turned it into a lamp. The little dents throw lovely shadows across my desk. I’m pretty sure one of those dents belongs to me.

mbm-0445.clue: I use the fallen leaves for captured pieces.
mbm-0445.quote: On windy days I put a leaf down where each captured chess piece used to stand. After our last park game the board looked like a neat little autumn. My opponent kept the leaf from his queen.

mbm-0446.clue: My first square became a window.
mbm-0446.quote: My crochet practice square had a lovely round hole in the middle. I made four sides and a roof to go with it. My niece’s toy mouse now lives in a house with a view.

mbm-0447.clue: I borrow my bookmark from the biscuit tin.
mbm-0447.quote: I saved a ribbon that once tied a box of shortbread and slipped it between the pages of my favorite novel. Whenever a chapter ends badly it helps to know there’s a biscuit color waiting on the next page.

mbm-0448.clue: I made a plate for a very particular pear.
mbm-0448.quote: I pressed the foot of a pear into soft clay and glazed the resulting hollow green. One pear sits perfectly upright in it. Every Saturday I go fruit shopping with an unusually demanding plate in mind.

mbm-0449.clue: I keep a drawer for words I haven’t used.
mbm-0449.quote: I write odd, wonderful phrases on paper scraps and file them in a desk drawer. One blew out and stuck to the window. It described rain, and the rain arrived before I’d got up to fetch it.

mbm-0450.clue: I like the net with the red repair.
mbm-0450.quote: A friend fixed one square of our volleyball net with red yarn. I use that tiny square as my target when I practice sets alone. The net gives me one bright friend to aim for.

mbm-0451.clue: I read the route from my bell.
mbm-0451.quote: I tied our canal map to my bicycle bell with a bit of blue string. At the first wrong turn the string tapped my brake lever. I took it as a very polite suggestion to look at the map.

mbm-0452.clue: I made a quilt from my dad’s paint shirts.
mbm-0452.quote: I cut out the patches with the best splashes and arranged them like flowers. The one patch with five blue fingerprints became the bird perched above the garden.

mbm-0453.clue: I draw a spiral on the scorecard.
mbm-0453.quote: On the practice green I play outward from the hole, one pace farther after each successful putt. My little score diagram looks like a snail. I’ve learned the patience to match it.

mbm-0454.clue: I saved the ribbon from our canoe bow.
mbm-0454.quote: My aunt tied a yellow ribbon there for my first trip on the river. It snapped free and caught in a willow downstream. Picked it up on the way home, like a message from the morning.

mbm-0455.clue: I recognize that bend by the red door.
mbm-0455.quote: There’s a canal lock with a red shed that reflects in the water. I take one photo from my kayak every season. In the winter picture I get that red door twice, once on the bank and once in the water.

mbm-0456.clue: I keep one yellow bead on the string.
mbm-0456.quote: At the weight room I move a wooden bead for each finished set. The little yellow one comes last. On a good day I hear it click against the rest before I remember I’m tired.

mbm-0457.clue: I read one chapter with a map open.
mbm-0457.quote: I traced the route in an old travel memoir on my atlas. At the end the pencil line made a loop around my own town. I went outside and walked one extra block for the author.

mbm-0458.clue: I found my favorite plane in a puddle.
mbm-0458.quote: The hangar doors were closed but the tail of a yellow training plane showed upside down in the rainwater underneath. I sketched the reflection. The mechanic opened the doors for the rest of the picture.

mbm-0459.clue: I save my last kick for the rainbow.
mbm-0459.quote: At our outdoor pool the gardener waters the hedge during the last morning lane session. I try to reach the wall just as the spray makes a rainbow. Once I touched the blue tile with all seven colors overhead.

mbm-0460.clue: I drew the bird after it left.
mbm-0460.quote: A little bird landed on my wet sketchbook, then flew off before I could count its wing bars. It left a trail of sharp little prints. I drew the rest of my memory around those careful little feet.

mbm-0461.clue: I turn the paddle into a measuring stick.
mbm-0461.quote: At the canoe picnic stop my friends argue about how deep the river is. I dip the paddle straight down and count the wet inches. The river leaves a different answer every visit.

mbm-0462.clue: I let the teacup pick the banker.
mbm-0462.quote: We keep the game money in three upside-down cups and shuffle them. Whoever lifts the one hiding a walnut is banker for the night. We’ve played whole evenings before remembering to put the walnut away.

mbm-0463.clue: I can fit a whole train on a bookmark.
mbm-0463.quote: I paint one little passenger window each time I see the evening local. The strip of card is nearly full. I’m going to need a very long novel if the train keeps adding carriages.

mbm-0464.clue: I quilted my sister’s first garden.
mbm-0464.quote: I stitched her crooked carrot rows just as they grew. One orange carrot has a little forked foot. That’s the one she pulled up on the day she decided she could garden after all.

mbm-0465.clue: I keep the worn end on my left.
mbm-0465.quote: I’ve played the same claves at our son circle so long that one has a little hollow at the grip. If somebody hands them to me backward I can feel it before the first note.

mbm-0466.clue: I wrote the date inside my shoe.
mbm-0466.quote: I rolled my first clean game in a pair of ugly orange bowling shoes. I wrote the date inside one. They’ve lasted through new laces, new soles and a very long run of less impressive scores.

mbm-0467.clue: I rehearse with a spool of thread.
mbm-0467.quote: My singing teacher dangled thread in front of my mouth so I could see how gently I was breathing. On the quietest note it barely stirred. I kept the little wooden spool as my smallest audience.
